A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SSA research work. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables and figures, support comparison despite localized formatting overlaps in v3.

before.justification: v2 reports original transformer experiments on quantification, linear-function ICL, NLP benchmarks and BabyBERTa linguistic probes.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results and adds evaluated baseline results and uncertainty reporting.

M1.justification: Equation 5 retains the same normalized signed-power scoring function and proposed trainable b/n family. Per-head parameterization and initialization are newly documented; the reported decoder exponent-setting revision is covered under E3.

E1.justification: Reported perplexity evaluation changes from FineWebText to OpenWebText in Section 7.2; OpenWebText previously appeared only in the token-norm diagnostic. Other task and dataset coverage is retained. The revised sigma ranges in heatmap captions match plots already present in v2 and do not establish added test scenarios.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds Sparsemax and Entmax to the existing linear-function comparison. Temperature-scaled Softmax, hybrid scoring, CosFormer, SA-Softmax and LLaMA were already evaluated in v2 and remain present.

E3.justification: Perplexity is now described as evaluation on a separate corpus. v3 also removes the decoder's explicit fixed n=1.5 setting and describes learned per-head parameters in Appendix B. Appendix A.2 specifies AdamW with a 6e-4 peak learning rate, versus v2's blanket Adam/1e-4 statement. These are reported setting revisions; reruns are not established, and Appendix B's general wording is not reconciled with the retained fixed-exponent BabyBERTa experiments.

E4.justification: The component ablations, model-size comparisons, deviant-input examples, LLaMA cases and distribution-shift plots are retained. New Appendix G reports uncertainty for existing benchmark results rather than a distinct robustness analysis.

E5.justification: v2 provides NLP benchmark point estimates; v3 Table 4 first reports mean plus or minus standard error across seeds throughout the zero-shot and three-shot suite. This substantially expands uncertainty reporting. Seed counts and identifiers are unspecified, so an increase in training runs cannot be established.

E6.justification: Table 1 adds Sparsemax and Entmax results, including MSEs of 78.16 and 81.74 at sigma=10, alongside unchanged SSA 8.50 and Softmax 45.35. Existing benchmark accuracies, BabyBERTa scores and plots are unchanged. Table 2 adds percentage-gain claims, including an incorrect 6.5% for LAMBADA's 24.8 to 25.4 increase, approximately 2.4%. The retained perplexities 31.7/27.7 are attributed to OpenWebText rather than FineWebText.

T1.justification: v2 contains the SSA formula and short limiting-case arguments. New Appendix J adds extensive derivative and ratio calculations, entropy and Lipschitz bounds, Jacobian analysis, and a bounded-logit non-collapse theorem. This is substantial new formal content, although several mathematical claims are incorrect.

C1.justification: The principal claims remain that Softmax contributes to ICL generalization failures, SSA mitigates these failures, and SSA improves small-model NLP performance. Rewriting and added supporting material do not redefine the main contributions.

C2.justification: v3 links gains on RTE, WiC and WSC to contextual reasoning, while Appendix J connects asserted gradient and entropy properties to stability, robustness and reduced overconfidence. It removes v2's limitation about being unable to train n for all tasks, while retaining the model-scale ceiling and failures under simultaneous input/function shifts.

D1.justification: Appendices A–B substantially expand reproducibility information: encoding/readout maps, dropout, curriculum schedule, GPT-2 dimensions and context length, optimization, batching, distributed mixed-precision training, hardware, runtime and SSA parameter initialization/overhead. These largely document existing experiments. Some detail is lost, including v2's explicit five-million-word BabyBERTa corpus description; the code address is unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds Sparsemax, Entmax and temperature-scaling references and discussion, plus sources for OpenWebText, GPT-2 and several retained benchmarks. The overall positioning around ICL limitations and Softmax saturation remains. The FineWeb bibliographic update refers to the same work.

P1.justification: The introduction, related work, SSA explanation, NLP discussion and conclusion undergo substantial rewriting. Related work gains thematic headings, Section 3 reorganizes task descriptions and motivation, and the appendices gain a substantially revised organization.

P2.justification: Table 1 gains rows and grid rules; Table 2 gains green percentage annotations, smaller text and removal of its perplexity row; new Table 4 redisplays benchmark results with uncertainty. Existing plots are reused and relocated, including the base-function plot moved into Appendix J. Heatmap captions are corrected, while new equations and headings overlap columns on pages 16–17.

improvement.justification: v3 improves reproducibility details, baseline coverage and uncertainty reporting. However, new Appendix J introduces substantive correctness problems: J.3's entropy lower bound fails, J.5 incorrectly claims exponential growth of normalized Softmax Jacobians, and J.6 incorrectly asserts divergence under fixed positive logit gaps. Table 2 also introduces erroneous percentage gains. These documentation and comparison benefits coexist with harms to scientific reliability, while seed and experimental-setting ambiguities remain unresolved. A reliable net quality direction is therefore unclear.
